verdict.why: Y is the better implementation base. Design §1 audits current and target routes from analysis through acceptance. REQ-4 and T9 test the owner's actual unit of spend: one HTTP request per validator, even on failure. X R9 instead permits a retry when no billed usage was returned; a timeout is not proof the first request was free. Y routes new decisions back to meanings regardless of spec size, whereas X R3–R5 invent a size-S exemption. Y also gives the operator a stronger rollout: check ledger writability before spending, verify BYOK against provider fixtures, preserve prior panel and judge rows on reruns, and compare canary quality with a baseline (Design §5; Rollout 2–6). X is stronger on the explicit Fable/Opus role assignments, unresolved-role preflight and unknown-cost reporting (Design role table; R1, R13–R16), but its unconditional addition of router and upstream cost is not justified by the measured zero-router-cost case. Its Q4–Q17 also leave tactical answers marked pending.
risks: Y Design §§2, 4 lets a missing map restore the superseded single-model rule, permits a legacy six-member panel, and checks judge identity after spend. Rollout 4 configures the intended estate, but a missing or stale file can undo that choice. Validate the owner's role routes, five families and judge before the first POST.

Y Design §5 can book absent BYOK cost fields as zero. Its proposed manual correction also cannot clear an original successful null-cost row: C6 still fails that row. Preserve unknowns and specify linked corrections that reconcile without double counting.

Y Design §6 allows an Observatory cache of any age after a failure; without a month check, last month's spend can drive this month's warning. Neither Y Rollout 7 nor X R18 proves the owner can actually see day and month totals in Observatory: both stop at a board row. Verify the displayed totals and warning before declaring rollout complete.

Y's ID tags verify coverage, not meaning. Design §4 gives the judge the source meanings only when `--meanings` is supplied. Require that input for split-spec reviews so the canary's fidelity counts are interpretable.
